svg.title: the first release stamps the version into every file that tracks it — the first release lands the tag, the changelog and the version bump
svg.text: the first release stamps the version into every file
Scenario: the first release lands the tag, the changelog and the version bump

g.text: Given a freshly generated project sitting at version 0.1.0
A brand-new project starts at version 0.1.0 — both its VERSION file and its Helm chart say
0.1.0 — and the developer has just committed a feature worth releasing.
When the first release bumps the version
task release runs Commitizen, which reads the feature commit, sees a new feature and moves
Then VERSION and the Helm chart both carry the new 0.2.0
The new number 0.2.0 is written into VERSION and into the Helm chart, so the machine and the
deployment agree on which version this is.

text.tspan: git show HEAD:VERSION ; git show HEAD:iac/helm/Chart.yaml

g.text: And it stamps a plain 0.2.0 tag and opens the changelog
The release also stamps a git tag that is just the number with no v in front (the cz.yaml
tag_format $version), and opens the changelog with a 0.2.0 section.
